result.summary: This PR introduces an experimental `testsubmitpackage` RPC for validating single transactions or 1-parent-1-child (1p1c) transaction packages against mempool policy and package RBF rules without modifying mempool state. It updates `ProcessNewPackage` and `MemPoolAccept` in the mempool validation pipeline to support dry-run package feerate calculations and sibling eviction evaluation, and returns predicted replacements.
result.problem: Wallets and second-layer applications lack an RPC to dry-run package submission (CPFP fee bumping or package RBF) to test if a package will be accepted and what it will replace before committing it to the network.

open_concerns: Author noted that downstream LN implementations often have parents paying sufficient fees due to trimmed HTLCs, making the restricted 1p1c design potentially insufficient
dergoegge noted user demand should be explicitly confirmed before deciding to maintain the endpoint
ismaelsadeeq suggested refactoring the dry-run path in ProcessNewPackage into its own function to avoid branching

result.card: Draft PR adding a testsubmitpackage RPC to validate 1p1c parent-child packages without mutating the mempool. Intended as a pre-flight check for wallets performing CPFP fee bumps and RBF evaluation, partially addressing issue #32160. It rejects packages where the parent passes individual acceptance on its own to avoid complex mempool unrolling logic. While reviewers support the concept, the author paused development to gauge external user demand, and the PR currently needs a rebase after several months of silence.
